title: Presence is modelled as a totally-ordered scalar but is at least three independent axes
description:
PresenceLevel is an ordered enum, None < Session < Software < Hardware, deriving Ord. At least three independent properties are being squeezed onto that one line, and none of them can be recovered from a single value.

AXIS 1 — who. FIDO2 UP is a capacitive tap and proves a finger, not a person; UV is a PIN or biometric and proves the enrolled user. Tracked separately as persona-3tly.2.

AXIS 2 — instant versus continuously maintained. A FIDO2 tap is a snapshot that starts decaying the moment it happens. A CAC or PIV card left inserted is a maintained state whose end is a DETECTABLE EVENT: PC/SC delivers card-removal, and DoD workstations already lock on it. Those are different security properties and the second is the stronger answer to 'right now', because the daemon can assert continuity through an observed interval instead of guessing a TTL. Today both land on PresenceLevel::Hardware and a consumer cannot tell them apart.

AXIS 3 — when, and how stale. persona-ogiv.

WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN THEORETICAL: the Ord derive is now load-bearing. persona-grpc/src/service.rs:167 folds requirements across audiences with .max(), which is what makes the persona-5s4b.47 fix order-independent and therefore unbypassable. Turning presence into a struct with independent axes means 'strictest' stops being a total order, and the fold needs a defined join — a lattice rather than a max — or the .47 property silently weakens. Anyone taking this must not break that.

CONCRETE CASE THIS BLOCKS, and it is the likely real-world answer for government deployments: a PIV attestor that watches PC/SC insertion and removal can say 'this card has been present continuously since T1'. That is a materially stronger claim than any tap, and the type system currently has nowhere to put it. persona-attestors/src/piv.rs is a 70-line stub, so the attestor that would produce it is unwritten too.
